children.topic: Acute Calculous Cholecystitis
Primary Pathology: Persistent cystic duct block by stone
Gold Standard Imaging: Abdominal Ultrasound (stones, thick wall > 4 mm, pericholecystic fluid)
Treatment of Choice: Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy (Early: < 72h; Late: interval in 6 weeks)
Acute Emphysematous Cholecystitis
Primary Pathology: Virulent infection by gas-forming Clostridia/E. coli in diabetics
Gold Standard Imaging: CT Scan / Ultrasound (gas bubbles in wall/lumen)
Treatment of Choice: Immediate Emergent Cholecystectomy (Surgical Emergency!)
Acute Acalculous Cholecystitis
Primary Pathology: Bile stasis + low-flow wall ischemia in critically ill ICU patients
Gold Standard Imaging: Abdominal Ultrasound / HIDA Scan
Treatment of Choice: IV Antibiotics + Urgent Cholecystectomy (if stable) or Percutaneous Cholecystostomy (if unstable)
Biliary Dyskinesia
Primary Pathology: Achalasia of Sphincter of Oddi (does not relax when GB contracts)
Gold Standard Imaging: ERCP (shows classic "pen-point" sphincter)
Treatment of Choice: ERCP Sphincterotomy (Cholecystectomy is strictly contraindicated!)
Porcelain Gallbladder
Primary Pathology: Chronic calcification of the gallbladder wall
Gold Standard Imaging: Coronal/Axial Abdominal CT scan
Treatment of Choice: Prophylactic Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy (Due to high adenocarcinoma risk)
